html:
A fast dance music created around 2002 and 2003 by Ivorian DJs in Paris, led by Douk Saga, and taken up in Abidjan nightclubs during the civil war.

Its name comes from slang for cheating and running off. Performers showed off by throwing money at the crowd, a style called travaillement, and songs made up new dance steps every season. It offered a party mood in grim years and spread across West and Central Africa and the diaspora. Like Congolese rumba before it, it made Abidjan a capital of African pop. Later Ivorian styles grew out of it.
sum: A fast dance music created around 2002 and 2003 by Ivorian DJs in Paris, led by Douk Saga, and taken up in Abidjan nightclubs during the civil war.
